You’re nitpicking. Millions of jobs have already been lost or transformed because of automation, and now AI is accelerating that same pattern. Bringing up pilots or printing machines doesn’t really address the point. Some jobs still require human involvement, sure. An accountant may still be relatively safe because there’s judgment, liability, and regulation involved. But try justifying the same level of human input in fields like animation, illustration, writing, editing, or basic design work. Yes, 3D printing machines are expensive and have a steep learning curve. But AI is different: it’s relatively cheap, accessible, and easy to use. You don’t need specialized equipment or years of technical training. You just describe what you want, and it produces something usable. That makes the disruption much broader and much faster.
